faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly mechanical engineering salary to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours, then by 52. For a full-time role at 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $33.71 per hour × 38 × 52 = $66,825 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a mechanical engineer under the Professional Employees Award?

faqs.q: Does the mechanical engineering salary include superannuation and casual loading?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Mechanical Engineering Salary

If you're working as a mechanical engineer in Australia, your pay may be set by an award, an enterprise agreement, or a individual contract. This guide helps you convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, using the latest Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission data. We'll also cover the National Minimum Wage, award minimums, casual loading, and how superannuation fits in.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

To estimate your annual gross pay, use:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week (the standard under most awards), the calculation is straightforward. For example, if your hourly rate is $33.71 (the minimum for a Level 1 graduate mechanical engineer under the Professional Employees Award 2020), your annual salary would be:

$33.71 × 38 × 52 = $66,825

If you're paid fortnightly, divide the annual figure by 26. For the same example, that's $66,825 ÷ 26 ≈ $2,570 per fortnight. Weekly pay is annual ÷ 52, or about $1,285.

This formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. Use our [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly breakdown instantly.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most mechanical engineers are covered by the **Professional Employees Award 2020**, which sets higher minimum rates. For example:

- Level 1 Graduate (3-year degree): $33.71 per hour
- Level 2 Experienced professional: $39.77 per hour
- Level 3 Senior professional: $43.46 per hour
- Level 4 Experienced medical research employee: $49.02 per hour
- Level 5 Experienced medical research employee: $59.05 per hour

These rates are the minimum; many mechanical engineers earn above award, especially with experience. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 annually. That's well above the award minimums, reflecting market rates for experienced professionals.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual mechanical engineer, you receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate instead of paid leave entitlements. For a Level 1 graduate, the casual rate is $33.71 × 1.25 = $42.14 per hour. The Fair Work Commission confirms this loading applies on top of the national minimum wage for award/agreement-free employees.

Superannuation is paid on top of your base salary. From 1 July 2026, the Super Guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a full-time mechanical engineer earning $66,825, super adds $8,019 per year. Note that super is not included in the hourly rate you see; it's an additional cost to your employer.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a $66,825 salary, the tax would be approximately $11,092 plus Medicare, giving a take-home of around $54,000. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a detailed estimate.

### Comparing Your Mechanical Engineering Salary

To see where your pay sits, check the [reference tables](/data) for award rates and ABS averages. The Professional Employees Award also includes penalty rates for weekend and public holiday work, plus overtime at time-and-a-half or double time. These can significantly boost your annual earnings if you work non-standard hours.

Remember, the conversion here is an estimate. Your actual pay may differ due to enterprise agreements, salary packaging, or other factors. Always refer to your pay slip and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) for your specific award.

### Key Takeaways

- **Hourly to annual**: Multiply by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks.
- **Fortnightly**: Annual ÷ 26.
- **Minimum rates**: National Minimum Wage $26.44; Professional Employees Award starts at $33.71 for graduates.
- **Casual loading**: Add 25% to base rate.
- **Super**: 12% on top, up to $270,830.
- **Tax**: Use the 2026–27 resident scale with Medicare.

For a quick calculation, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool. It handles casual loading and shows annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures.
